summary.name: What is SRE (Site Reliability Engineering)?
summary.one_liner: An O'Reilly article, drawn from Google's SRE book, explaining release engineering and how it supports Site Reliability Engineers in running reliable services.
use_cases: Understanding the role of a release engineer
Learning how Google makes software releases repeatable
Planning canary and rollback strategies for deployments
Setting up policy and access control for release steps
summary.what_it_does: The page explains release engineering as the discipline of building and delivering software, and describes how Site Reliability Engineers depend on repeatable, automated release processes. It outlines Google's release engineering philosophy: a self-service model where teams run their own releases, high-velocity frequent releases, and hermetic builds that depend only on known tool and library versions. It also covers cherry picking to rebuild older releases with targeted fixes, and layered policies that gate approvals, deployments and build configuration changes, with automated change reports to aid troubleshooting.
notable: Describes Google's hermetic build approach, where builds are insensitive to host-installed software
Covers cherry picking to patch old releases using versioned build tools
Explains a 'Push on Green' model that deploys every build passing all tests
caveats: Describes Google's internal practices; not a general tool or how-to guide
Article text is a conceptual overview with no step-by-step instructions
